header.text: Merchants traveling along different sections of the Silk Road encountered different environments. In order to move goods across diverse environments, merchants needed to use different types of transportation. Read the passage about how merchants transported goods along the Silk Road. Then answer the question below.

pieces.text: Merchants used

, or animals that carried heavy loads, to move goods along the Silk Road. Parts of the Silk Road were deserts that had few sources of water. So, camels were well-suited to work in deserts because they could walk for many days without water. Other parts of the Silk Road crossed high mountains and flat fields. Merchants used donkeys in high mountains and flat fields because they worked well in these environments.

table.text: People traded luxury goods, such as glass and silk, across Europe, Asia, and Africa. Goods traveled all the way from the Han Dynasty in China to the Roman Empire in Europe.

The Mongol Empire controlled territory across Asia, the Middle East, and Europe. As a result, Mongol rulers controlled most of the Silk Road, and trade between Europe and Asia increased.
